messages:
incident-bot: [ALERT] 5xx rate increase detected for /v1/generate (prod, us-west) — 2m window. p95=1.2s -> 3.8s, p99=0.4s -> 6.2s. Trigger: canary deploy 2026-03-15T15:08Z by deploy-bot commit abcdef1. Pager: @Maya (oncall)
Maya (oncall): I'm oncall, looking. Opening grafana and logs now: https://grafana.internal/d/serving/latency?orgId=1&var-service=frontend
Ravi (runtime): that's my canary. I pushed a runtime change that adjusted keepalive / heartbeat behavior for multiplexed streams (commit abcdef1). On my side I see a spike in proxy timeouts to model-workers ~15:08.
Kai (platform): joining. Noted 5xx and gateway 502s in the edge. Can you paste the deploy id?
deploy-bot: Canary deploy started: service=frontend-runtime, commit=abcdef1, canary_weight=10%, started=2026-03-15T15:08:22Z
Maya (oncall): quick check — metrics-bot, recent error counts?
metrics-bot: last 5m: total requests 1.2M, 5xx_count=14.8k (1.2%), error spike started 15:08Z, peaked at 15:11Z.
Maya (oncall): ok. Ravi — do you see errors in runtime logs? Any stack traces?
Ravi (runtime): yes, grpc proxy logs show repeated read timeout while waiting for stream frames. Snippet:```
[15:09:37Z] proxy/frontend -> worker: read timeout after 30s, connection reset by peer
[15:09:38Z] worker/xyz: keepalive ping failed, write: broken pipe
```
Ravi (runtime): Also seeing KV cache pressure and increased eviction rates around same timeframe. Could be the keepalive change interacting poorly with our multiplexing in the runtime router.
Mike (SRE): This looks like a classic heartbeat/stream boundary regression. If canary is at 10% and we're seeing customer impacting errors, we should yank the canary to safe. Paging ops: @Jen can you prepare rollback path?
Jen (ops): on it. Two options: quick rollback via deploy dashboard (set canary weight 0) or k8s scale down. Which do you prefer?
Ravi (runtime): dashboard rollback is fine. We need the revert to happen fast; keep the rollback-only change (don't roll forward the whole pipeline).
Maya (oncall): initiating rollback via Console -> Deploys -> frontend-runtime -> rollback canary -> confirm. ETA ~20-40s.
deploy-bot: Rollback action requested by Maya (oncall): target=frontend-runtime canary, action=rollback-to-stable, initiated=2026-03-15T15:11:05Z, change_id=rb-20260315-01
Kai (platform): I'm watching ingress and proxy stats. Increasing 502s now but starting to dip after rollback initiation? need to confirm.
Maya (oncall): running quick check command:```
# tail recent 5xx entries
curl -s 'https://prod-logs.internal/api/query?service=frontend&since=10m' | jq '.[] | select(.status>=500) | {ts:.ts, route:.path, status:.status, msg:.message}' | head -n 6
```
Maya (oncall): sample output shows lots of `stream read timeout` and `upstream reset` lines.
Ravi (runtime): I'm going to immediately revert the keepalive change in staging and create an infra hotfix branch so we don't accidentally re-promote it.
deploy-bot: Rollback completed: target=frontend-runtime canary, result=success, completed=2026-03-15T15:11:45Z, change_id=rb-20260315-01
Maya (oncall): metrics quick check: p99 dropped from 6.2s -> 0.6s within 60s of rollback. 5xx rate dropping back toward baseline.
Mike (SRE): Confirmed on SLO dashboard: error budget impact estimated ~0.04% for 5m window, customer-visible errors lasted ~7 minutes at worst. No large SLA breach but definitely customer impact for some calls.
Kai (platform): Ingress proxies exhibited elevated connection resets to worker pool while canary was live. Looks like the new keepalive semantics caused stale stream markers and some backpressure that triggered worker-side connection closures.
Jen (ops): I've created an incident channel: #incident-5056789012 and started a skeleton postmortem doc: https://docs.internal/incidents/5056789012. Adding immediate actions: rollback confirmed, EM to notify support.
Maya (oncall): Handoff: I'll keep this thread for live mitigation notes. Assigning follow-ups: Ravi -> RCA and revert PR, Kai -> add canary runbook guard (require streaming-canary smoke check), Mike -> SLO/alerts tuning to catch p99 spikes earlier, Jen -> customer comms & incident doc.
Ravi (runtime): Initial hypothesis: heartbeat/keepalive change in abcdef1 altered how zero-byte frames are interpreted by the proxy, causing delayed frame boundaries and worker-side timeouts under multiplexed loads. Repro in dev with synthetic load. Creating PR to revert now: https://git.internal/redwood/frontend/compare/revert-abcdef1
Maya (oncall): ops checklist: 1) rollback done 2) verify canary weight = 0 3) monitor for recurrence 4) create postmortem draft 5) schedule RCA session.
Mike (SRE): I'll add a new canary health check: require p99 < 1s and 5xx < 0.2% for 5m before promotion beyond 10%. Also will add alert that breaks longer than 3x median p95 in 2m trigger auto-rollback.
Kai (platform): Also adding a temporary guard to block that specific commit from re-promoting until RCA complete.
Jen (ops): Support notified, ticket created for impacted customers where we saw repeated 502s. UX team informed in case of spike of support cases.
Maya (oncall): closing live mitigation loop: system stable, metrics trending normal. We'll leave this thread attached to incident doc; will move to postmortem when draft is fleshed out. Thanks everyone. :white_check_mark:
incident-bot: Incident record created: id=INC-5056789012, severity=sev2, created=2026-03-15T15:12:30Z
metrics-bot: follow-up note: peak affected requests ~18k in 5m window, unique customers impacted ~42, sustained errors ended after rollback and subsequent 3m of stabilization
Ravi (runtime): sending PR to revert and adding extra unit/regression test for stream heartbeats.
Mike (SRE): next steps: RCA meeting tomorrow 10am, add timeline to incident doc, assign owners.
Jen (ops): assigning postmortem owner: Ravi.
Maya (oncall): handing off to Ravi and Jen for post-incident work. I'll ping if anything flakes.
Ravi (runtime): acknowledged. Will keep thread updated with PR and RCA notes.
Maya (oncall): thanks all — great quick response. :bow:
